user.title: TomTom Setup
user.description: Name this entry and choose how it should be searched. An area or a tracker reads TomTom's traffic incidents in its circle; a route from start to destination is worked out by TomTom on every poll, with the traffic of the moment, and reports what it runs through.

key.title: TomTom API key
key.description:
Everything here comes from TomTom, which needs an API key - free, no payment method:

1. Sign up at [developer.tomtom.com]({url}).
2. Right after that, **API & SDK Keys** in the dashboard already lists a key, *My First API key*, with every API enabled - the Traffic API, the Routing API and the Search API among them, the ones used here. Copy it with the button beside it.
3. Paste it here.

One key serves every entry of this Home Assistant. If one is already saved, leave the field empty to keep it.

route_defaults.title: Defaults for new routes
route_defaults.description: What every new route starts with: on the card, a route planned there is saved with these settings straight away; in the setup wizard they are filled in and can still be changed. The days and hours are the ones the route is kept up to date in, and the way back can be made along with it - driven at another time of day, with hours of its own.

data.live_days: Days the route is kept up to date

data_description.return_route: A second entry, destination to start - on a motorway the way back is the other carriageway, and a jam on one is not one on the other. Named after this entry, with "return" added.

data.only_certain: Only reports TomTom is sure of
data.roads: Only these roads (comma-separated road numbers, e.g. A8, B2)

data_description.only_certain: TomTom rates every report: certain, probable, risk_of or improbable. A jam measured from moving cars is certain, a roadwork from a road authority probable, a driver's single report a risk. On, the first two are kept; off, the uncertain ones come along too.
data_description.roads: Only reports TomTom files under one of these road numbers, A8 or B2 - the motorways of a commute without every side street along it. Case and spaces do not matter. Empty keeps every road.
data_description.blacklist: Reports to leave out, by TomTom's incident id - the id or short_id attribute of a report's entity, shown in its details. TomTom's own apps do not show it.

sources.title: Data sources
sources.description:
Further sources of reports beside TomTom, for every entry at once. A source adds only what TomTom has not got, under kinds of its own in each entry's list, so no report stands there twice.

**blitzer.de** reports speed cameras and traffic checks, fixed and mobile, in Germany and its neighbours. No key and no account; it reads what the site's own map reads, which blitzer.de has not published as an API and may change or close. Every request is counted under **blitzer.de this month**.

**Lufop** reports speed cameras, fixed, mobile and red-light, and section controls, from its radar database - a documented API with a free personal key from [api.lufop.net](https://api.lufop.net/). A request answers one country; the free plan covers France, Belgium and Switzerland, 200 requests a day and 200 radars a request. Every request is counted under **Lufop today**.

data_description.lufop_api_key: Checked when it is given and when Lufop is switched on; one already saved is kept by leaving the field empty.
data_description.lufop_country: The one country every entry asks Lufop for - the free plan allows France, Belgium and Switzerland.

entry_failing.title: {name} is not delivering
entry_failing.description:
The TomTom entry **{name}** has failed {count} polls in a row, so its entities are unavailable. The last reason:

`{reason}`

A tracker without a position, or a tracker entity that no longer exists, is fixed under the entry's **Configure**; a refused key under **Configure** on the TomTom Settings entry; if TomTom itself cannot be reached, this clears on its own once it can. This repair goes away with the next poll that succeeds.

quota_at_risk.title: The {api} quota will not last the month
quota_at_risk.description:
{used} of {tier} free **{api}** requests after {days} days; at this pace about **{projected}** by the month's end, more than {percent} % of the tier.

Fewer polls help: a longer update interval, tighter hours on a route, the traffic flow on fewer cards.

This goes away when the pace drops below the share set under TomTom Settings → Configure → Quota warning → TomTom, and with the new month.

quota_day_at_risk.title: The {api} requests of the day are nearly used up
quota_day_at_risk.description:
{used} of the {tier} requests a day the **{api}** plan allows are used.

The day's requests are shared by every entry of this installation - and by anything else that uses the same key. Fewer polls help: a longer update interval, tighter hours on a route, or Lufop switched off for the entries that lie outside its country.

This goes away at midnight UTC, when Lufop's day turns, or when the share set under TomTom Settings → Configure → Quota warning → Lufop is raised.

quota_day_used_up.title: The {api} requests of the day are used up
quota_day_used_up.description:
All {tier} requests a day of the **{api}** plan are used - Lufop counts everything that uses the same key. It refuses further requests until midnight UTC - {reset} here.

Fewer polls help tomorrow: a longer update interval, tighter hours on a route, or Lufop switched off for the entries outside its country.
